Ability search/list returns compact catalogue entries; use exact ids for full interface details and applicability. Search results are indexes. Exact queries return one record per offset. All paged records use600-code-unit fragments with zero-based part0..parts-1, consistently in proactive and queried views. Current-scope retained queries are reprojected using these stable pages; original results remain archived. Queries expose no hidden properties, other private records or historical capabilities. Queries do not perform physical trials or award experience. Exact-id queries return a complete record of up to 6000 code units as one value in a single result; larger records keep the paged form. Paged records omit their per-record notes: concatenate all parts before parsing; continue with the same exact id. An entry marked inRetrieval is shown with at least the same content under the same id in this input's retrieval. observation.terrain rows are "y:x:cells" strings: each character of cells is the terrain kind of one visible cell, at x, x+1, ... in row y. abilities.baseline entries with id, function and args summarize interfaces you neither used in the last 25 rounds nor need now. args lists the arguments in order: a bare name is a string; otherwise its type with any bounds (number>=lo, integer<=hi, integer lo..hi, and a bare lo..hi is a number range) or its choices a|b; ? marks an optional argument and "" means none. value.name: Beam mass comparator
value.function: Assess, assemble, test, use, inspect or dismantle a lever comparator: your branch beam across a stone fulcrum, a fixed seat and your own sliding reference piece. Readings give sample mass as a fraction of the reference and before/after ratios, as intervals.
value.costs: Study: 4 rounds, 0.5 energy each. assess (materialIds, supportIds, referenceId, sampleId, or comparatorId): 1 round, 0.2; reports each requirement met or missing. assemble: materialIds [beam: your whole untreated branch unit; optional fulcrum: your whole stone or flint unit, set where you stand on firm ground], or supportIds [a solid stone or flint object in reach], and referenceId (your non-food piece that does not decay, at most 1 unit): 3 paid rounds of 0.5, continuing; resume with assemble and comparatorId. test, compare: one reading, 1 round, 0.2, at your comparator; reading empty or loaded (sampleId: your unreserved item, at most 1 unit); approach outward or inward. inspect: 1 round, 0.2. dismantle: 1 round, 0.2. Checks run before any charge; gather, pickup and travel are separate; no refund.
value.effects: Assumed: a branch is a uniform 1.1 m beam laid at its midpoint; positions are fractions of the half-beam from the fulcrum (+ toward the reference), read to 0.02; the seat is at -0.9. A reading slides the reference until the beam tips: torques of the actual masses against stiction 0.005 m x mass on the fulcrum, so outward and inward tips bracket a null range. A test (3+ empty and 3+ loaded readings of one sample, both directions each) passes if each set repeats within 0.04 and closes; a new test replaces it. compare on a tested comparator: an empty check, 3+ loaded readings of one sample (both directions) and a closing empty check within 0.04 of the test give an endpoint: sample/reference = (null - empty null)/0.9 as an interval. A later endpoint of the same sample (followed through pickup, cutting or exposure) and reference gives after/before: decrease or increase only if it excludes 1, else inconclusive; a wet stone or flint reference adds 1%, other wet references are inconclusive. Rain voids a test; a fulcrum losing firm ground damages it. Parts keep their ids and return on dismantle. No grams, water, safety or reward.

execution.progress: Assembly continues each round; an unworked round pauses it, keeping placed parts, and assemble with comparatorId resumes after rechecks. Other modes take one round.

value.name: Compare prepared material samples
value.function: Take a small sample and equal reference from your own food; split or slice the sample with your stone or flint edge onto a clean support in actual weather; weigh both on your tested beam comparator; tend; stop.
value.costs: Study: 4 rounds. start: sourceItemId, your unspoiled whole berry or root stack; sampleQuantity 0.1-1 (default 0.1; over twice it must remain); durationRounds, exposure window (default 10); 1 round, 0.2 energy. prepare: preparation; toolId, your carried whole stone or flint unit with a usable edge; supportId, your clean, dry, rigid, non-toxic item (a whole unit per 0.04 covered) laid at location in reach on firm clear ground, or a food surface in reach; 1 round, 0.5. measure: measurementDeviceId, your tested beam-mass-comparator in reach, weighs the sample and the reference; 1 round, 0.2 per item. tend: in reach; location moves your support and pieces; 1 round, 0.2. stop: 1 round, 0. Checks precede any charge; travel, gathering and comparator work cost separately.
value.effects: Start separates sample and reference with tenths, decay, harvest time, origin and the world water record (assumed root 0.75, berry 0.85); both stay whole, carried, reserved. Prepare cuts the sample, taken as a 1000 kg/m3 sphere, into 2 halves or slabs of at most 5 mm laid cut face up (at least 0.04 per unit); no mass, wear or offcut; opening damage 1.1. Each round only lying cut faces exchange water: rate h/1200 x (saturation vapour density at the face - humidity x that of the air), h = 10 x (1 + 0.5 wind), face temperature from the heat balance with latent heat 2.45 MJ/kg, bounded by free water above the humidity equilibrium within 0.33 mm; rain adds 0.01 x rain x area; dry matter and nutrition stay. A weighing slides the reference both ways: mass as a reference fraction at 0.02 resolution against the tested tare; repeats give after/before and reference-adjusted intervals, a change only if 1 is excluded, else unresolved. No water content is shown. The window ends completed (weighed) or indeterminate; spoilage, removal, stop or death end it early, releasing the reference once; pieces and support stay. No preservation, safety or reward.

execution.progress: One atomic round per mode; lying cut pieces keep exchanging water unattended, without charge.
